name: Devin

runner.notes: Preferred harness path: install Devin CLI (curl -fsSL https://cli.devin.ai/install.sh | bash, or brew install --cask devin-cli), sign in with a Devin account, cd into runs/<run-id>/worktree and run `devin -p --prompt-file prompt.md` (add `--respect-workspace-trust false` for non-interactive runs in an untrusted dir). Record the model/Adaptive/Fusion selection, permission mode, and whether --sandbox was used. GUI path: Devin Desktop (ex-Windsurf) Agent Command Center with Devin Local on a worktree session. Devin Cloud (`devin --cloud`, web app, API) runs in a Cognition VM and must be reported as a separate cloud lane, not mixed with local runs. Third-party ACP agents inside Desktop measure the guest agent, not Devin.

inclusion: Included as Class A (with a Class B cloud lane noted). Cognition's Devin is no longer only the cloud autonomous engineer: since 2026-06-02 Windsurf is Devin Desktop, whose primary view is an Agent Command Center (Kanban of local and cloud agent sessions, Spaces, git-worktree sessions with merge) that also runs third-party agents (Codex CLI, Claude Agent, OpenCode, Gemini CLI, Junie) via ACP, plus a local Devin CLI/Devin Local agent harness. That local multi-agent cockpit is a direct peer of Class A ADEs (compare GitHub Copilot app, Warp, JetBrains Air). The flagship Devin Cloud (brain always in Cognition's cloud; VM devboxes; enterprise dedicated VPC) is an enterprise agentic platform and should be benchmarked and reported separately from local runs.
runtime_model_notes: Primary path is first-party (Devin Local/CLI locally, Devin Cloud in Cognition VMs; Cascade legacy through July 2026); Devin Desktop also hosts third-party ACP agents with billing and terms delegated to the guest vendor.
pricing_model: Self-serve Free ($0, light quota), Pro ($20/mo, up to 10 concurrent cloud sessions), Max ($200/mo, unlimited concurrency), Teams ($80/mo minimum; $40/mo full seat incl. Devin Desktop, free flex seats; up to 200 users); quota shared across Devin Cloud, Desktop, CLI and Review with on-demand credits after quota. Enterprise is contract-priced in Agent Compute Units (ACUs) with dedicated deployment options.
public_stack_signals: Devin Desktop is the renamed Windsurf IDE (VS Code-derived user data directory; Chromium/Electron caches referenced in migration docs); installers for macOS, Windows, and Linux tar/deb/rpm (package devin-desktop).

Devin CLI is a local terminal agent for macOS, Linux, WSL, and Windows; supports non-interactive --print mode, ACP server mode (`devin acp`), cloud session control (`--cloud`), and an Outposts worker mode.
Devin Cloud architecture: stateless 'brain' always in Cognition's cloud; per-session 'Devbox' VM (Ubuntu, Windows, macOS) with shell, browser, and VS Code-based IDE served via *.devinapps.com.
REST API v3 (organization and enterprise scopes) with service users (cog_ keys); official Devin MCP and DeepWiki MCP servers.
capabilities_to_probe: Devin CLI headless single-task correctness on the v0.1 fixtures
Devin Desktop Agent Command Center parallel worktree sessions and merge
ACP guest agents (Codex/Claude/OpenCode) inside Devin Desktop
managed Devins parallel fan-out in Devin Cloud
Devin Review auto-fix loop on PRs
CLI OS-level sandbox and permission modes
moat_hypotheses: Single vendor spans IDE (ex-Windsurf install base), local CLI agent, and autonomous cloud VMs with one quota and handoff between them.
Enterprise trust surface (SOC 2, ISO 27001, FedRAMP claims, dedicated VPC, CMK, federal docs) plus deep SDLC integrations.
Org knowledge layers (DeepWiki, Knowledge, Playbooks, Skills, Session Insights) accumulate customer-specific context.
setup_notes: Requires a Devin account for all agent paths; Free tier exists but quota is light, so budget a Pro plan for repeatable runs.
Keep local (CLI/Devin Local) and cloud (Devin Cloud VM) runs in separate result lanes; cloud runs clone from a git remote and do not see the local worktree.
Linux sandbox (--sandbox) requires bubblewrap and socat; it fails closed if missing.

sources.notes: Homepage: 'Devin runs in the cloud or on your machine, tests in its own browser'; surfaces Devin Cloud, Desktop/CLI, Slack/Teams/Linear/Jira, Devin Review, Security Swarm, DeepWiki; enterprise SOC 2/ISO 27001/FedRAMP, zero data retention, RBAC/SSO/SCIM, VPC deployments.

Free $0; Pro $20/mo (up to 10 concurrent sessions, Devin Cloud access, SWE-2 free in Desktop/CLI through 2026-10-10); Max $200/mo (unlimited concurrency); Teams $80/mo + $40 per full seat, up to 200 users; Enterprise contact sales with dedicated deployment option.
Full docs index (Cloud, CLI, Desktop, Enterprise, Federal, API) used to map product surfaces.
Devin as autonomous AI software engineer; workspace with Shell, IDE, Browser; web app app.devin.ai, API, Slack/Teams; CLI install and /handoff workflow.

Windsurf became Devin Desktop on 2026-06-02; Agent Command Center (Spaces, Kanban, multi-agent) is primary view; products unified as Devin Cloud, Desktop, CLI, Review; Desktop usable with local-only agents; Cascade retained through July; Devin Local replaces Cascade; local paths ~/.devin, ~/.codeium.
Kanban board of local agent sessions and cloud Devin sessions; status grouping; native notifications for Cascade, Devin Local, and ACP agents.

Third-party agents via Agent Client Protocol (Codex CLI, Claude Agent, OpenCode, Junie, Gemini CLI, custom); Pro/Max/Teams, enterprise by admin; guest billing/terms delegated to the third party; local and team ACP registries.
Devin Local shares the Devin CLI harness; subagents, OS-level sandboxing, plan mode, Quick Review subagent, worktree sessions with Merge; enterprise-gated by admin toggle.
Git worktrees under ~/.windsurf/worktrees/<repo>, post_setup_worktree hook, up to 20 worktrees per workspace with LRU cleanup.
Spaces group local and cloud agent sessions, PRs, files, and shared context per task.
Devin Desktop installers for macOS, Windows 10+, Linux tar/deb/rpm (glibc >= 2.28); package renamed devin-desktop with windsurf transitional package.
Devin CLI quickstart (curl installer, Homebrew cask, Windows installer); CLI is a local agent distinct from cloud Devin; CLI lacks Knowledge/Playbooks/Secrets support at review time.
Flags --print/-p, --prompt-file, --permission-mode, --sandbox, --cloud, --resume; `devin acp` stdio server; `devin cloud drs` blueprint commands; hidden `devin worker` for Outposts.
OS-level sandbox (macOS seatbelt, Linux bwrap+socat), fail-closed, not supported on Windows; network filtering marked unstable.
Managed Devins: coordinator session spins up child sessions in isolated VMs with ACU limits, messaging, sleep/terminate; playbook and knowledge management; schedules.
Hand off from Devin CLI (/handoff) or from Claude Code/Codex/Cursor via open-source club-cog/devin-handoff plugin using the Sessions API.

Brain always in Cognition Cloud; Devbox in Cognition multi-tenant cloud (Enterprise Cloud) or customer-dedicated single-tenant VPC via AWS PrivateLink/IPSec; Enterprise Assured adds customer-managed keys.
Outposts: cloud session tool execution on customer machines via `devin worker start`, outbound-only HTTPS; agent loop stays in Devin cloud; available on Pro/Max/Teams.
Self-serve plan mechanics: shared quota across Devin sessions, CLI, Desktop; Teams full vs flex seats; Pro includes Slack, Linear, MCP integrations.
Enterprise meters Agent Compute Units (ACUs); self-serve uses quota then on-demand credits; sessions sleep after 30 min idle; no concurrent session limits stated for metering.
Devin Review PR review platform for GitHub (incl. GHES), GitLab (incl. self-managed), Azure DevOps partial; Auto-Fix referenced in guidelines.
REST API v3 organization and enterprise scopes, service users with cog_ credentials, sessions on behalf of users.
Official Cognition GitHub org ('Makers of Devin'); product itself is closed source.

infrastructure: Local: Devin Desktop and Devin CLI run the agent harness on the user's machine against local files; inference via Cognition cloud with multi-vendor models (Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, Cognition SWE models, open models), Adaptive router and Fusion pairing.
Cloud: each Devin session runs on its own isolated VM with shell, browser, IDE, and computer use; environment configured by blueprints; sessions sleep after 30 minutes idle.
Enterprise Cloud (multi-tenant) or Customer Dedicated Deployment (single-tenant VPC over AWS PrivateLink/IPSec); Enterprise Assured adds CMK; federal deployment docs exist.
Outposts let cloud sessions execute tool calls on customer-owned machines with outbound-only HTTPS workers.

parity_risks: Hybrid runtime: ACP guest-agent runs measure the guest (Codex/Claude/OpenCode), not Devin; label runtime per run.
Local (CLI/Devin Local) and cloud (Devin Cloud VM) lanes have different environments; cloud runs need a git remote and cannot see the local worktree directly.
Model routing (Adaptive/Fusion/default) and promotional quotas (e.g. SWE-2 free until 2026-10-10) change over time; record model and plan.
Devin Cloud enterprise features (dedicated VPC, CMK, Outposts on dedicated tenants) are account-gated and not reproducible from a self-serve account.
CLI does not yet support cloud Knowledge/Playbooks/Secrets, so local and cloud context parity differs.

hypotheses: Owning IDE, local CLI agent, and autonomous cloud VMs under one account/quota with one-click local-to-cloud handoff is hard for single-surface Class A peers to match.
Windsurf install base plus enterprise contracts (ACU billing, dedicated VPC, federal) give distribution that local OSS ADEs lack.
Accumulated org context (DeepWiki, Knowledge, Playbooks, Session Insights) and review loop (Devin Review Auto-Fix) increase switching costs.
Opening Desktop to third-party ACP agents neutralizes the 'bring your own agent' advantage of guest-cli cockpits.
evidence: Official FAQ states products are unified under Devin (Cloud, Desktop, CLI, Review) and Desktop is the command center for local and cloud agents.
Official docs describe Agent Command Center, Spaces, worktree sessions, ACP guest agents, managed Devins, handoff, Outposts, and enterprise dedicated deployment.
Pricing page lists Free/Pro/Max/Teams self-serve tiers and an Enterprise tier with dedicated deployment.
unknowns: No harness run yet; single-task quality vs other Class A peers is unmeasured.
Durability of legacy Windsurf surfaces (JetBrains plugin in maintenance mode, Cascade sunset) and pace of Devin Local feature parity.
Actual concurrency, quota exhaustion behavior, and cost per fixture task on Free/Pro plans.
Enterprise-only controls and dedicated deployment behavior need account-backed verification.
